# 2.8.0

One additive capability: flow-paced streaming callbacks (backpressure for `cb(chunk)` streams).

- **`flowCallback(cb, opts?)` — the sibling of `endCallback`: one ends a stream, this one paces
  it.** A server method streaming through a client-supplied callback wraps it once; `push(chunk)`
  sends the frame exactly like `cb(chunk)` and resolves when the flow window allows more, so
  server memory stays O(chunk) against a slow client instead of growing without bound. Two
  independent signals: a negotiated credit window (`Caps.CB_FLOW`, on by default — the client
  runtime acks cumulatively after each frame's consumer call settles, promises included, so an
  async consumer paces the producer by its real speed; acks coalesce, never one per frame), and
  a local watermark fallback in the replay lag-gate vocabulary (`{pending, highWater, lowWater,
  pollMs}`, defaulting to a socket.io write-buffer probe) that an un-negotiated old peer gets
  automatically. Flow-declared streams deliver sequentially and the response waits for the
  stream's drain, preserving the callbacks-before-response ordering the synchronous path had.
  Disconnect, `endCallback`, or the method promise settling reject pending pushes with
  `MyError('E_FLOW_CLOSED')`. A callback that never traveled the wire passes through
  transparently; methods that never wrap their callback are byte-identical on the wire.
  Wire: `Pkt.CB_FLOW` (declaration, rides the ordered callback queue) + `Pkt.CB_ACK`
  (cumulative), negotiated via `opt.flowCallback`. Acceptance spec: `test:rpc-flow`.
